items.headline: Proposal for reconstruction of Karambar bridge
items.blurb: The PWD sent a ₹2 crore reconstruction proposal in March 2025 after a portion of the 1963 arch bridge sank on Wednesday on the MIA–Bajpe SH-67. A temporary earthen culvert with concrete pipes allows light vehicles while heavy vehicles use alternate roads; city–airport traffic is unaffected as the bridge lies beyond MIA.
items.why_channel: ₹2 crore Karambar bridge rebuild after partial collapse — direct airport-road infra hook for Mangaluru commuters.

items.headline: Railways to install double boom barrier at Pandeshwar Level Crossing
items.blurb: Palakkad Division, pending a road-over-bridge, will install a double boom-barrier at Pandeshwar Level Crossing at about ₹2 crore; tenders are open and work is expected to be finalised within a fortnight and completed in six months. MCC and the DC offered to widen a 200 m road stretch to four lanes when Railways widens the crossing; MLA Vedavyasa Kamath and MP Brijesh Chowta pursued the issue.
items.why_channel: ₹2 crore Pandeshwar level-crossing safety upgrade with six-month completion target — local commute and safety impact.

items.headline: Street vendors evicted in Hampankatta
items.blurb: Mangaluru City Corporation officials launched an eviction drive on Thursday evening against street vendors who had illegally encroached footpaths in Hampankatta and surrounding areas, removing flowers and temporary structures and warning of stringent legal action against repeat encroachment. Dakshina Kannada Zilla Beedhibadhi Vyaparasthara Sangha Honorary President B K Imthiyaz condemned the drive, saying flower vendors from Hassan, Mandya and other districts had come for Krishnashtami and that the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 permits vending during festivals.
items.why_channel: MCC Hampankatta vendor eviction vs festival livelihood rules — high-share civic clash on daily street life.

items.headline: Forest staff seek divine intervention to tackle elephant menace
items.blurb: Belthangady forest department staff offered ‘Rangapooja’ at the Sowthadka Shree Mahaganapathi kshetra in Kokkada, praying that wild elephants would not cause loss of human life or damage to agriculture. During 2026-27, over 80 wild elephants destroyed crops and areca plantations worth over Rs 77 lakh in Belthangady, Sullia and Kadaba taluks; Rs 3.30 lakh compensation was released to 19 people while Rs 73 lakh remained pending for 381, and forest officials have submitted a proposal to establish an elephant camp at Gundya.
items.why_channel: Rs 77 lakh crop damage from 80+ elephants in Belthangady belt — safety and livelihood stakes across coastal DK.

items.headline: Case filed against associate NCC officers of NITK over financial irregularities
items.blurb: Surathkal Police registered a case against NITK Associate NCC Officers Prof P Johnson and Prof H Shivananda after an internal Comptroller and Auditor General audit found TA/DA claim bills were based on false documents; the duo were detained and an internal investigation is underway. NITK Director B Ravi said the NCC unit must uphold morality and integrity, and appointed Dr Mohan Lal Meena, Assistant Professor in Chemical Engineering, as NCC caretaker officer in place of the ANOs.
items.why_channel: NITK Surathkal NCC TA/DA fraud case after CAG audit — accountability at a major Mangaluru institution.
